issues.quote: then restart the app once and watch its startup log
issues.text: The api runs from an image built by DonHang.Api/Dockerfile (`COPY DonHang.Api/ DonHang.Api/` then `RUN dotnet publish ...`), so a plain restart runs the old binary and never sees the edit. Executed: after adding the Console.WriteLine and `docker compose restart api`, "list ran" appeared neither at startup nor after two curls (grep count 0) - the promised "Both curls do print it, once each" does not happen. After `docker compose up -d --build api` the same steps gave 0 at startup and exactly 2 after the curls. The lesson also never says how to read the app's log.
issues.fix: Step 1: "... then rebuild and restart the app with `docker compose up -d --build api` from the repo root, and watch `docker compose logs api`." Step 2: "Once the startup lines end with no such line printed, run `curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products` twice and look at `docker compose logs api` again." Keep the expected result as written; it is exactly what the rebuild produces.

issues.quote: A method is attribute-routed when the method and its class carry attributes stating the HTTP method and the path
issues.text: Unlisted claim (nothing in .meta.json covers the definition of attribute-routed) and wrong as a general rule: the route template may sit entirely on the action, with no attribute on the class. The docs sample for attribute routing is `public class HomeController : Controller` with `[Route("")] [Route("Index")] [Route("/")]` on the methods only; routing.md:425 "Route templates that you apply to an action and that begin with `/` or `~/` don't get combined with route templates that you apply to the controller."
issues.fix: Write it as a description of this code, not a definition: "A method is attribute-routed when attributes state the HTTP method and the path right next to the code itself - in `ProductsController` the attribute on the class carries the path and the attribute on each method carries the HTTP method." Add the sentence to .meta.json claims (kind behavior, version_key aspnetcore).

issues.quote: the order between them only decides what is available to the app, not how a later request is answered
issues.text: As written the subject is "the order", so the sentence says the order decides what is available to the app. It does not: both registrations end up available whichever order they are written in. Claim 3 in the ledger only covers the second half ("does not affect how any individual request is later handled"), so the first half is an unlisted and incorrect statement that a junior can read as "order controls availability".
issues.fix: Rewrite: "When two calls register different things, as every call in this file does, the order between them decides nothing: both are available to the app either way, and neither order changes how a later request is answered." Check the same wording in the five-line summary item 2, which is already correct.

issues.quote: False, because `OrderService` and `JwtTokenService` are unrelated to `/api/v1/products` entirely.
issues.text: Option d is true of the repo: `ProductsController(DonHangDbContext db)` takes only the DbContext, and neither OrderService nor JwtTokenService takes any part in answering GET /api/v1/products. Two options (c and d) are therefore defensible for a reader who has read the code, and d's explanation rebuts a different statement ("Both lines are in Program.cs because the app needs both") - unrelated to the app is not what d says.
issues.fix: Give d a reason that is actually false, e.g. en: "False, because ASP.NET Core sorts the `Services.Add...` calls itself before the app starts, so the order they are written in is never used" (vi likewise), and change explanation.d to: "Nothing sorts or rewrites the registrations; they stay in the order written - the order simply has no effect on how a request is handled."

issues.quote: is what makes an **endpoint** exist at all
issues.text: True of this file (MapControllers is Program.cs's only endpoint-creating call), but phrased as a general rule it tells a junior that endpoints can only come from MapControllers. fundamentals/routing.md:80-83 lists MapRazorPages, MapControllers, MapHub<THub> and MapGrpcService<TService> as the calls that create endpoints.
issues.fix: Scope it to this app: "One of those wiring calls, `app.MapControllers()`, is what makes this app's **endpoint**s exist at all" (quiz q3 already scopes it correctly with "The one call in `DonHang.Api/Program.cs`").

issues.quote: register a database connection, a standard error format (`AddProblemDetails()`), an order service, and a way to issue tokens
issues.text: `AddDonHangInfrastructure(connectionString)` adds more than "a database connection": DonHang.Infrastructure/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs@stage-1 registers `AddDbContext<DonHangDbContext>(options => options.UseNpgsql(connectionString))`, `IOrderRepository -> EfOrderRepository` and `INotifier -> LoggingNotifier`. The list reads as one line = one thing, which is the undercount the previous round set out to fix.
issues.fix: Say what the line is without counting its contents: "... register the app's database access (that one call adds the database context and the classes built on it), a standard error format (`AddProblemDetails()`), an order service, and a way to issue tokens."

issues.quote: add a temporary `Console.WriteLine("list ran");` as the first line inside `ProductsController`'s method for `GET /api/v1/products`
issues.text: Step 1 tells me to edit `ProductsController`'s method for `GET /api/v1/products`, but the lesson never shows that class, never says which file it is in, and never shows one of the attributes it keeps talking about. A products class plausibly has more than one GET method; if I pick the wrong one the curls print nothing and I cannot tell whether the lesson is wrong or I am. Finding the right method is guesswork on top of the three minutes.
issues.fix: In Try it step 1, name the file (for example `DonHang.Api/Controllers/ProductsController.cs`) and add one clause saying the method to edit is the one whose attributes name GET and the path `/api/v1/products`.

issues.quote: A teammate points at a single line, `app.MapControllers();`, and says "that line is what makes the API answer `/api/v1/products`."
issues.text: "API" is a word I have not been given and the lesson never defines it. Everywhere else the lesson says "the app", so I stop to decide whether the API is the same thing as the app, something inside it, or something in front of it — the previous lesson did have a server in front answering with fixed strings.
issues.fix: In section 2 replace "that line is what makes the API answer `/api/v1/products`" with "that line is what makes the app answer `/api/v1/products`", the wording used in the rest of the lesson.

issues.quote: You do not see a URL anywhere near it.
issues.text: "URL" is not in what I know and is never defined. The very next sentence says "a specific path", a word the lesson uses consistently afterwards, so I have to guess whether URL and path mean the same thing here or whether I am supposed to be looking for two different things in the file.
issues.fix: Replace "You do not see a URL anywhere near it." with "You do not see that path anywhere near it."

issues.quote: a database connection, a way to issue tokens, and so on — gets registered on that one object
issues.text: "a way to issue tokens" — and the same phrase again in section 5, next to `JwtTokenService` — rests on "token", a word I have never met. I cannot tell whether a token is something the app stores, sends or checks, so the example of what gets registered teaches me nothing and I skip both sentences. It does not block the main idea, but it is the only example the lesson gives twice.
issues.fix: Gloss the word once at first use in section 4, e.g. "a way to issue tokens (the strings a client later sends back to prove who it is)", or replace both mentions with a phrase built from words the lesson already uses, e.g. "a way to prove who a caller is".

issues.text: Step 1 asks me to rebuild the container with `docker compose up -d --build api` and then wait for the startup log to settle before curling. A rebuild is not something that finishes while I watch it, so the "3 minutes" in the heading is optimistic the first time I run this.
issues.fix: Change the heading to "Try it (5 minutes)", or add "the rebuild takes a minute or two the first time" to the end of step 1.

issues.quote: read only its first and last lines for now; everything between them, comments included, belongs to later lessons
issues.text: The prose tells me to read only the first and last lines of the 23-line block, and the sentence right after the block explains a line in the middle of it. I had just been told I was not allowed to look there, so I read the block a second time to find the line being discussed.
issues.fix: Change "read only its first and last lines for now" to "read only its first and last lines plus the `app.MapControllers();` line for now".

issues.quote: When two calls register different things, as every call in this file does, the order between them makes no difference to how a later request is answered.
issues.text: The rule always arrives with a condition — calls that "register different things" — and the lesson never says what the other case is. The condition comes back in Beginners often think, in quiz q2 and in summary line 2, so by the fourth time I am sure the other case matters and I still cannot picture it.
issues.fix: Add one clause at the first use in section 4 saying the other case does not arise here, e.g. "two calls registering the same thing is a case this file does not contain and this lesson does not cover".

issues.quote: When `builder.Services.Add...` calls register different things, their order only decides what is available to the app, not how any request is handled.
issues.text: Line 2 reads as if the order is the thing that decides what is available to the app, which is the opposite of section 4's "the order between them makes no difference". I read it three times before deciding it must mean the calls, not their order, decide what is available.
issues.fix: Rewrite line 2 as: "`builder.Services.Add...` calls that register different things only decide what is available to the app; the order among them does not decide how any request is handled."

issues.quote: Between `Build()` and `Run()`, Program.cs does the rest of its startup work, including wiring up (through `app.Use...`/`app.Map...` calls) the steps every incoming request will pass through before reaching your code
issues.text: This one sentence carries four things: what happens between `Build()` and `Run()`, what wiring means, which calls count as wiring, and a forward reference. I re-read it twice. The same "that is the next lesson's subject" deferral then returns in Beginners often think, in Connections and in summary line 5.
issues.fix: Split it in two: one sentence for what happens between `Build()` and `Run()` and what the `app.Use...`/`app.Map...` calls do, one short sentence for the forward reference.

issues.quote: True, because a request always uses services in the same order they were registered in Program.cs.
issues.text: Options a and b state the same claim in two wordings, so both have to be wrong, and d invents a rule about "the compiled order of the assembly" that appears nowhere in the lesson. I can land on c by elimination without having understood anything about registration order.
issues.fix: Rewrite option b so it offers a different tempting reason, e.g. "True, because `AddSingleton` and `AddScoped` build their objects right at the registration line, in the order written."

issues.quote: which registered service a piece of code uses depends on what that code asks for, not on registration order
issues.text: The explanation for option b tells me which service a piece of code uses "depends on what that code asks for". Nothing in the lesson says code asks for services, so the sentence meant to correct me hands me a new idea I have no way to check.
issues.fix: Reword b's explanation using only what the lesson says, e.g. "the order of these two calls decides what is available to the app, not how any request is handled".

issues.quote: restarts the app once, and is confused not to see it print in the startup logs
issues.text: The question has the junior "restart the app once" after editing the code, but Try it made a point of rebuilding with `--build` because a plain restart does not pick the change up. In the question's own story the line would therefore not run at all, which made me hesitate over option d before picking a.
